data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel's reliability is superior only when the checklist atomizes the expert's 'gestalt' into discrete, verifiable facts; the distinguishing evidence of reliability is the presence of 'negative-constraint' adherence in the face of intuitive pressure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The trap items are so obscure they are perceived as errors in the checklist itself, leading to erratic marking.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel is trained to prioritize 'completion' over 'accuracy' in the checklist process.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Trap-Item' Filter: To distinguish reliability from compliance, the checklist must include 'trap items'\u2014criteria that are objectively false for the case but 'feel' true based on common misconceptions. Genuine reliability is evidenced when the panel marks these items 'False' despite the intuitive pull to mark them 'True' to complete the pattern. Mere compliance would show a 'True' marking to maintain the perceived flow toward the correct final answer.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
